counterfactual_missing_items: No explicit phrase 'atrial septal defect' is written in the vignette, so the diagnosis is inferred from the defect plus shunt and oxygen step-up
No ASD subtype (e.g., ostium secundum, primum, or sinus venosus) is specified
No right ventricular oxygen saturation or Qp/Qs ratio is documented to quantify shunt magnitude beyond the structural defect
decisive_items: Step-up in oxygenation from superior vena cava (71%) and inferior vena cava (77%) to right atrium (84%)
Dilated right atrium and right ventricle
response.rationale: R2 integrates the structural defect, left-to-right shunt, oxygen step-up at the right atrium, and right heart dilation into a single coherent diagnosis. R1 only captures the ECG RBBB finding, which is an associated conduction abnormality rather than the underlying defect causing the shunt; it does not explain the major hemodynamic and imaging evidence. C1 merely restates RBBB with nearly identical raw support, so it adds no independent diagnostic value. The margin is high because the pivotal raw evidence all points to R2 over R1/C1.

rejected.why: The only raw support is the ECG right bundle-branch block, which is a secondary finding and not a complete explanation for the large defect, left-to-right shunt, oxygen step-up, or right-heart dilation.
It is a correlated append-only restatement of R1 using the same raw span, so it adds no independent or more complete diagnostic evidence.
